      "contextStartEvent": 49,
      "contextEndEvent": 235,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "if it weren't for feelings and cultural indoctrination getting in the way, every atheist on the planet would agree with me.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity", "ridicule"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The universal explanation of disagreement substitutes an attributed psychological defect for establishing why every atheist's objection fails. E94–235 subsequently offer an analogy and skepticism argument, but do not establish this universal diagnosis. The explicit attribution of all dissent to feelings or indoctrination protects the conclusion; it is not itself a compact slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 248,
      "endEvent": 254,
      "contextStartEvent": 161,
      "contextEndEvent": 315,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "If secular humanists had a drop of real skepticism coursing through their veins, they'd have to abandon their position.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity", "ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The catchphrase makes abandoning secular humanism a test of possessing genuine skepticism. E161–235 argue for equal scrutiny, but do not establish that every secular humanist position fails it; E255–315 address objective morality specifically. Calling continued adherents devoid of real skepticism supplies both the missing universal verdict and protection against their objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1285,
      "endEvent": 1290,
      "contextStartEvent": 1137,
      "contextEndEvent": 1313,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "is in no way relevant to whether or not they were they would care about a better world.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The categorical dismissal could exclude behavioral counterevidence to the claim that people care about improvement. However, A distinguishes wanting improvement from acting effectively and proposes follow-up interviews and education at E1291–1313. Whether this excludes relevant evidence regardless of merits or makes a defensible distinction remains uncertain; no slogan replaces the argument."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2707,
      "endEvent": 2714,
      "contextStartEvent": 2690,
      "contextEndEvent": 2749,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "you're going to pay for that one way or another in some sense.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The maxim answers an undetected-theft hypothetical by guaranteeing personal costs. Prices and markets supply a proposed mechanism at E2712, but not proof that every theft costs its perpetrator enough to defeat self-interest. The unrestricted wording suggests protection, yet E2729–2749 concede negligible impact and distinguish secular humanism from pure selfishness."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2824,
      "endEvent": 2829,
      "contextStartEvent": 2754,
      "contextEndEvent": 2830,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I don't believe you. So it wouldn't work on me. That's the proof of it.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Disbelief is presented as proof against the proposed solution, potentially making A's own refusal sufficient to reject it. However, E2827–2830 explicitly mirror B's personal-conversion argument and distinguish working from being better. This may be a limited counterexample to universal persuasion rather than insulation against the merits of God's alleged foundation."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2983,
      "endEvent": 2987,
      "contextStartEvent": 2957,
      "contextEndEvent": 3003,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "we can manipulate and redefine the goal as we need",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Redefining the goal to ensure constant improvement could make contrary results irrelevant by changing the success criterion. Yet E2957–2983 emphasize fallible intuitions, evidence, and discovery, while E3648–3692 expressly allow substantial error and only likely improvement. The text leaves uncertain whether this is protective goal-changing or ordinary revision through learning."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3322,
      "endEvent": 3339,

      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B asserts divine permission to kill and invokes possible foreknowledge of beneficial consequences, potentially shielding lethal commands from criticism through unseen benefits. However, E3340 explicitly disclaims that consequentialist explanation as his own view; E3341–3378 offer covenant distinctions and specific commands. A blanket protection device is therefore not securely established."
    }
